units.en: The ⟦0⟧ is a landlocked minor country in Central Asia with a population of ⟦1⟧. It is bordered by ⟦2⟧ in the south and east; ⟦3⟧ in the west; the ⟦4⟧ in the north; and ⟦5⟧ in the far northeast. The country's strategic location along the Silk Road connected it to the cultures of the Middle East and other parts of Asia.

The political history of the modern state of Afghanistan began with the Hotak and Durrani dynasties in the 18th century. In the late 19th century, Afghanistan became a buffer state in the "Great Game" between British India and the Russian Empire.

Following the 1842 defeat of the British-Indian forces and victory of the Afghans, the British established diplomatic relations with the Afghan government and withdrew all forces from the country. They returned during the Second Anglo-Afghan War in the late 1870s for about two years to assist Abdur Rahman Khan defeat Ayub Khan. The United Kingdom began to exercise a great deal of influence after this and even controlled the state's foreign policy.

After the Third Anglo-Afghan War and the signing of the Treaty of Rawalpindi in 1919, King Amanullah Khan declared Afghanistan a sovereign and fully independent state. He moved to end his country's traditional isolation by establishing diplomatic relations with the international community and, following a 1927–1928 tour of Europe and Turkey, introduced several reforms intended to modernize his nation

The reforms quickly alienated many tribal and religious leaders. Faced with overwhelming armed opposition, Amanullah Khan was forced to abdicate in January 1929 after Kabul fell to rebel forces led by Habibullah Kalakani. Prince Mohammed Nadir Shah, Amanullah's cousin, in turn defeated and killed Kalakani in November 1929, and was declared King Nadir Shah. He abandoned the reforms of Amanullah Khan in favor of a more gradual approach to modernisation but was assassinated in 1933 by Abdul Khaliq, a Hazara school student.Mohammed Zahir Shah, Nadir Shah's 19-year-old son, succeeded to the throne and reigned from 1933 to 1973.
Afghanistan maintained its neutrality in World War II.
Main article: Afghan national focus tree
⟦0⟧ gets a unique national focus tree as part of the ⟦1⟧ expansion. Without the expansion, Afghanistan utilizes the ⟦2⟧.
The Afghan national focus tree can be divided into 5 branches and 11 sub-branches and 1 joint branch:

This industrial branch focuses on bonuses to the economy and improving the ⟦0⟧ national spirit. It includes research slots, factories and railroads, but will force the player to answer to the demands of the graduates who need jobs as well as the rural folk. It also allows selling oil to foreign powers, or gaining aid from the ⟦1⟧. Continuing with the latter will unlock the ⟦2⟧ Sub-branch.

This ⟦0⟧ sub-branch installs a pro- ⟦1⟧ government and grants bonuses to army, propaganda and industry courtesy of Moscow. Then, it allows the player to gain Central Asian territories from the ⟦2⟧ and core it. It also grants expansion opportunities into ⟦3⟧.
This shared focus between the ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ paths give weekly ⟦2⟧
This ⟦0⟧ branch focuses on keeping the King without a ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧ civil war, and opens the two consequent sub-branches.

This sub-branch rids King Zahir Shah of his uncles' interference, and allows a closer cooperation with the West, modernizing and getting bonuses to economy, research and army, as well as allowing the establishment of a ⟦0⟧, including potentially ⟦1⟧. It also grants a war goal on ⟦2⟧.
This shared sub-branch between the historical and democratic branches give increased ⟦0⟧ with foreign majors, ⟦1⟧ and a division.
This historical sub-branch creates a balancing act between the ⟦0⟧ and the ⟦1⟧, including the ability to expel nationals of either. It also builds a dam and allows some modernization.
This branch explores alternative monarchist paths.

This alternative ⟦0⟧ branch brings back the reformist yet vengeful Amanullah Khan as leader, allowing modernization and bonuses to the army, economy and resources. Then, the branch becomes very aggressive, allowing expansion into ⟦1⟧, the ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧. The ultimate goal here is to become the savior of Islam and to achieve the Pashtunistan Ascendancy.
Request German Support/Contact Rural Maliks Sub-branch These focuses request help from Germany, or rural leaders in the event of a civil war.
Instead of supporting Amanullah Khan as the leader of Afghanistan, the player may decide on alternative leaders. It also creates a faction with other middle eastern nations and calls ⟦0⟧ for aid.

Crown the Golden Emir Sub-branch This Crowns Faqir of Ipi as the Emir of Afghanistan. It supports rebels in central Asia, demands India's North western states, and forms the Emirate of Pashtunistan. It also gives War Goals for Islamic states.

Crown the Bukharan Emir/Invite the Mughal Prince Sub-branch This either crowns Sayyid Mir Muhammad Alim Khan as the Emir of Afghanistan, or Mizra Khurshid Jah Bahadur as Mughal Emir. The Player can either expand into the Soviet Union as the Second Afghan Empire or reform the Timurid Empire and reclaim its borders.

This military branch focuses on bonuses to the army and improving the ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ national spirits. The Quami side focuses on cavalry, irregular infantry, and equipment capture, while the Nufus side allows development of infantry equipment, armor and purchase of planes. Both sides can help with the intelligence agency and developing stronger mountain battalions.
It gives as dockyard and naval expansion should ⟦0⟧ gain a coastline.
Align with the Allies/Pursue Our Own Agenda/Seek Alternative Partnerships Branch

This foreign politics branch allows ⟦0⟧ to configure its foreign policy, benefitting from and balancing each of the ⟦1⟧ and the ⟦2⟧. The ⟦3⟧ side allows participating in Operation Countenance, expansion into ⟦4⟧, establishing a ⟦5⟧ buffer state, as well as gaining territory from ⟦6⟧. The central part gives a choice between either confederating with ⟦7⟧ or conquering it. Meanwhile, the ⟦8⟧ side will give bonuses to the army courtesy of ⟦9⟧ and ⟦10⟧ and culminates in the ⟦11⟧.
This joint branch shared with ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ builds up the ⟦3⟧ national spirit with industry an military bonuses.

At the start of both the 1936 and 1939 scenarios, Mohammed Zahir Shah of the Barakzai royal family is the leader of Afghanistan. His non-aligned party is overwhelmingly popular in both scenarios, but that popularity wanes slightly in favor of the fascist party in 1939, which, like the remaining political parties in Afghanistan, has a generic name and randomized leader.
